subject: Materials Science
title: Ultrasonic Testing: Sound Finds Flaws
description: A micro-lesson that makes Ultrasonic Testing: Sound Finds Flaws usable.

hook.text: A doctor uses ultrasound to see a baby. An engineer uses it to see cracks inside steel.

buildup.text: High-frequency sound waves enter the material — flaws reflect the waves back as echoes.

discovery.text: The time delay and echo strength reveal a defect's depth, size, and orientation inside the part.

twist.text: Rough surfaces and coarse grain structures scatter sound waves — not every material is easy to inspect.

climax.text: Every aircraft landing gear, every rail weld, every pressure vessel is ultrasonically inspected before service.

punchline.text: Sound waves find what eyes can't see — flaws hidden deep inside solid metal.

quiz.question: How does ultrasonic testing detect internal flaws?
options: By heating the material and watching for hot spots
By sending sound waves that reflect off defects as echoes
By magnetizing the material and checking for field leaks
